characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.description: A detective discussing Porlock and Professor Moriarty with Inspector MacDonald; he has sent money to Porlock twice and has never met Moriarty.

characters.name: Watson
characters.description: The narrator and a doctor who feels annoyed by Holmes's interruption and called Moriarty a criminal.

characters.name: Moriarty
characters.description: A professor and celebrated author of The Dynamics of an Asteroid, described by Holmes as a brilliant schemer and leader of the underworld.

characters.name: Porlock
characters.description: A man using an assumed name who sent a letter from Camberwell prophesying a crime and has received money from Holmes twice.

characters.name: Watson's companion

characters.name: Professor Moriarty
characters.description: A wealthy and calculated individual who earns six thousand a year and maintains high financial secrecy through numerous bank accounts.

characters.name: Holmes
characters.description: A detective or investigator who receives secret advance information from Porlock and discusses Professor Moriarty with Watson.

characters.name: Narrator
characters.description: The first-person narrator ('I') who observes Holmes, inspects the cipher paper, and converses with Holmes.

characters.name: Douglas
characters.description: A murdered man whose death Holmes suspects was orchestrated by Moriarty or one of his subordinates.

characters.name: The Speaker
characters.description: The unnamed individual engaged in conversation with Watson, capable of reading ciphers.

characters.name: Billy
characters.description: A page who brings the expected letter to Holmes and Watson.

characters.name: Fred Porlock
characters.description: The author of a note warning that he is being watched and suspected, who asks the recipient to burn a cipher message.

characters.name: John Watson
characters.description: Holmes's companion and narrator, who suggests 'The Bible' as the mystery book Holmes is seeking.

characters.name: MacDonald
characters.description: A man who insists on immediately travelling to Birlstone to pursue the case and gives the group five minutes to prepare.

characters.name: Inspector MacDonald
characters.description: An inspector with an Aberdeen upbringing who visited the professor to discuss eclipses and is investigating the Birlstone mystery.

characters.name: Mr. Holmes
characters.description: A clever detective addressed by Inspector Alec MacDonald, who worked with Dr. Watson to solve a cipher.

characters.name: Dr. Watson
characters.description: The narrator of the passage who scrawled an enigmatic message on a paper and solved a cipher alongside Mr. Holmes.

characters.name: Alec MacDonald
characters.description: A young, trusted inspector and member of the detective force, characterized by a tall, bony frame, keen intelligence, dour nature, and a hard Aberdonian accent.

characters.name: Mr. Douglas
characters.description: A man associated with Birlstone Manor House who was horribly murdered.

characters.name: The Professor
characters.description: A man in London with a thin face, gray hair, and a solemn manner of speaking who prophesied a crime before it occurred.

characters.name: Jean Baptiste Greuze
characters.description: The artist who painted the picture of a young woman hanging in Professor Moriarty's room.

characters.name: The Inspector
characters.description: An official detective investigating the Birlstone Mystery who confers with Sherlock Holmes.

characters.name: Jonathan Wild
characters.description: An 18th-century master criminal who operated as the hidden force behind London criminals on a 15% commission.

characters.name: Mr. Mac
characters.description: An inspector and self-described practical man who has a cab ready to take him and Holmes to Victoria.

characters.name: Colonel Sebastian Moran
characters.description: Moriarty's chief of staff, described as aloof, guarded, and inaccessible to the law.
